venues.name: 230 Fifth Rooftop

venues.name: Attaboy
venues.cover: None listed (1 source)
venues.hours: Daily 5pm–3am
venues.howto: Limited reservations on OpenTable (parties of 6 and under); everyone else first-come, first-served; ring the buzzer at the unmarked 'AB 134' door; expect a wait late and on weekends

You want food or a menu to browse: there is no food and no drink menu, just a conversation with the bartender.

venues.name: Beauty & Essex
venues.cover: None listed (restaurant/lounge); optional $86/pp set menu, whole table must participate (1 source)
venues.hours: Closed Mon; Tue–Wed 5–10pm; Thu 5–11pm; Fri–Sat 5pm–midnight; Sun 5–10pm
venues.howto: Reservations on OpenTable (parties up to 14; 15+ email the venue); 24-hour notice for cancellations
venues.subway: Delancey St–Essex St (F, J, M, Z), about 2 blocks south, ~3 min walk; station not currently step-free (1 source)
skip: You want a late night: it closes by 10–11pm most nights and midnight on Fri–Sat, and is closed Mondays.
You're on a budget: OpenTable lists it in the top $$$$ tier and cocktails run about $20 each.

venues.name: Bossa Nova Civic Club
venues.cover: Varies by night: free or suggested donation on some weeknights; around $15 cash reported for regular nights; RA tickets for bigger lineups (unconfirmed)
venues.age: 21+ with driver's license, non-driver ID or passport (1 source)
venues.hours: Seven nights a week, roughly 10pm–3:30/4am (varies by event) (unconfirmed)
venues.howto: Walk up and pay at the door; some nights sell advance tickets on Resident Advisor; bring cash (1 source)
venues.subway: Under the elevated M on Myrtle Ave; Central Av (M) is the nearby stop, ~1–3 min walk (unconfirmed)
skip: You want room to move: the dance floor is small and sits between the bar and the bathrooms, so traffic is constant.
You dislike heavy fog and a dark, cramped layout, which reviewers call out.

venues.name: Brooklyn Mirage
venues.status_note: Brooklyn Mirage never reopened after its 2025 renovation (DOB structural/safety issues; no 2025 season), and owner Avant Gardner filed Chapter 11 in Oct 2025. Pacha's parent FIVE Holdings took over in early 2026 and the site reopened as Pacha New York, a seasonal open-air club (June–Oct 2026; 'Open Air Season Closing' listed for Oct 18, 2026). A year-round indoor room, Brooklyn Pacha, opens in the Great Hall at the same address on Nov 6–7, 2026.
venues.cover: Not applicable (closed); successor Pacha New York sells tickets per event
venues.age: Successor Pacha New York: 21+ (per individual event listings) (1 source)
venues.hours: Not applicable (closed). Successor's open-air season ran June–October 2026
venues.howto: Brooklyn Mirage is closed. For the same site, buy advance tickets for Pacha New York / Brooklyn Pacha events (DICE; brooklynpacha.com for the indoor room) (1 source)
venues.subway: Not found yet
skip: You're looking for the Brooklyn Mirage itself: it no longer exists under that name; the site is now Pacha New York.
You want a sure thing in the off-season: the open-air venue is seasonal (June–October) and big nights sell out in advance.

venues.name: Death & Co
venues.cover: None listed (1 source)
venues.hours: Sun–Wed 6pm–1am; Thu–Sat 6pm–2am
venues.howto: Walk-ins always welcome and mostly first come, first served; limited reservations on SevenRooms; parties up to 8, no standing room, 2-hour limit. Door takes your number and texts when a seat opens.
venues.subway: F at 2 Av (Lower East Side–Second Ave) or 6 at Astor Pl; roughly 7–12 min walk (1 source)
skip: You hate waiting: seating is mostly first come, first served and peak-hour waits can run long (reviewers describe leaving a number and being called back).
You want to stand and mingle or stay all night: no standing room and a 2-hour cap per visit.

venues.name: Elsewhere
venues.cover: Ticketed per event; Oct 2026 listings ran about $10–36, with some headliner tiers up to ~$100. Door tickets after the event starts have no fees (1 source)

skip: You dislike lines and crowds: reviewers advise queuing early for weekend rooftop parties, and the Hall holds about 600.
You want a polished cocktail experience: it is a loud, large warehouse venue with drinks served in plastic cups.

venues.name: Employees Only

venues.subway: 1 to Christopher St–Sheridan Sq (a short walk west on Christopher to Hudson) (1 source)
skip: You want a quiet drink: reviewers say it gets crowded and loud at peak hours, and late-night crowds can get rowdy.
You hate lines: the bar is walk-in only and reviewers report waits at the door.

venues.name: Good Room

You want a non-ticketed drop-in: most nights are ticketed RA parties, so check the calendar first.

venues.name: Harriet's Rooftop
venues.cover: None listed; a suggested 20% gratuity is added to checks (discretionary, can be changed on request)

skip: You want a quiet, cheap drink: it is a busy, view-driven hotel rooftop popular with tourists, with a 20% gratuity added to checks.
The weather is bad: the rooftop opens weather permitting, so check Instagram first.

venues.name: House of Yes

venues.name: Knockdown Center
venues.cover: Ticketed per event; prices vary by act (e.g. ~$59 listed for Cortex & Adrian Younge, Oct 12 2026) (1 source)
